title: Daemon-Role Credential Scoping: GitHub App vs Fine-Grained PAT
summary: Prior-art survey for backlog #3872 (epic #3383) — how to give the conveyor's now-daemonized processes (a read-only watcher, e.g., a narrower GitHub credential than a write-capable daemon, e.g. the Fix-dispatch or Review daemon). Confirms today's status quo: every daemon inherits the SAME single GitHub OAuth token from `gh auth login` (repo+workflow scoped, no per-process narrowing exists in the code today). Surveys the real mechanics of GitHub Apps' per-installation-token scoping (permissions + repositories narrowed per mint, one-hour expiry, but `gh` CLI itself has no native App auth) against GitHub fine-grained personal access tokens (scoped at creation to specific repos and a fixed permission set, up to 366 days, zero code change needed since `gh` already honors a per-process `GH_TOKEN` env var). Recommends fine-grained PATs per daemon-role as the pragmatic near-term default, with GitHub Apps as the concrete upgrade path if a real incident or infrastructure change (e.g. moving off a single operator laptop) raises the stakes.
